description: A target row joining more than one source row makes a merge-UPDATE non-deterministic and Snowflake refuses it (ERROR_ON_NONDETERMINISTIC_MERGE default TRUE, Duplicate row detected during DML action) with the target untouched and no duplicate falling through to WHEN NOT MATCHED; the rule is UPDATE-specific and clause-sensitive - the same duplicate join runs with only WHEN MATCHED THEN DELETE, and with a WHEN MATCHED AND that narrows the duplicates to one source row. Converted 1:1 from dml/MergeMultiMatchTest (now retired).

steps.sql: CREATE TABLE tgt (id INTEGER, v VARCHAR)
CREATE TABLE src (id INTEGER, v VARCHAR)
MERGE INTO tgt USING src ON tgt.id = src.id WHEN MATCHED THEN UPDATE SET v = src.v WHEN NOT MATCHED THEN INSERT (id, v) VALUES (src.id, src.v)

error.messageContains: Duplicate row detected during DML action

steps.sql: MERGE INTO tgt USING src ON tgt.id = src.id WHEN MATCHED AND src.v = 'a' THEN UPDATE SET v = src.v
MERGE INTO tgt USING src ON tgt.id = src.id WHEN MATCHED THEN DELETE
